"So I did, so I did; that's the fifteenth umbrella or so that Verneede has annexed of mine: what does he _do_ with them, do you think, Belinda?"

arxiv-2105-03596.title: Dynamic-OFA: Runtime DNN Architecture Switching for Performance Scaling on Heterogeneous Embedded Platforms
arxiv-2105-03596.creator: Wei Lou, Lei Xun, Amin Sabet, Jia Bi, Jonathon Hare, Geoff V. Merrett University of Southampton, UK {wl4u19, lx2u16, ms4r18, J.Bi, jsh2, g.merrett}@southampton.ac.uk
arxiv-2105-03596.description: Abstract Mobile and embedded platforms are increasingly required to efficiently execute computationally demanding DNNs across heterogeneous processing elements. At runtime, the available hardware resources to DNNs can vary considerably due to other concurrently running applications. The performance requirements of the applications could also change under different scenarios.

arxiv-2204-01880.title: Models and Mechanisms for Spatial Data Fairness
arxiv-2204-01880.creator: Sina Shaham, Gabriel Ghinita, Cyrus Shahabi
arxiv-2204-01880.description: Abstract . Fairness in data-driven decision-making studies scenarios where individuals from certain population segments may be unfairly treated when being considered for loan or job applications, access to public resources, or other types of services. In location-based applications, decisions are based on individual whereabouts, which often correlate with sensitive attributes such as race, income, and education.

arxiv-2205-04464.title: Differentiable Electron Microscopy Simulation: Methods and Applications for Visualization
arxiv-2205-04464.creator: Ngan Nguyen, Feng Liang, Dominik Engel, Ciril Bohak, Peter Wonka, Timo Ropinski, Ivan Viola
arxiv-2205-04464.description: Abstract We propose a new microscopy simulation system that can depict atomistic models in a micrograph visual style, similar to results of physical electron microscopy imaging. This system is scalable, able to represent simulation of electron microscopy of tens of viral particles and synthesizes the image faster than previous methods.

arxiv-2304-14937.title: Contactless hand tremor amplitude measurement using smartphones: development and pilot evaluation
arxiv-2304-14937.creator: James Bungay, Osasenaga Emokpae, Samuel D. Relton, Jane Alty, Stefan Williams, Hui Fang, and David C Wong
arxiv-2304-14937.description: Abstract Background - Physiological tremor is defined as an involuntary and rhythmic shaking. Tremor of the hand is a key symptom of multiple neurological diseases, and its frequency and amplitude differs according to both disease type and disease progression. In routine clinical practice, tremor frequency and amplitude are assessed by expert rating using a 0 to 4 integer scale.

arxiv-2309-05466.title: Development of the CMS detector for the CERN LHC Run 3
arxiv-2309-05466.description: Abstract Since the initial data taking of the CERN LHC, the CMS experiment has undergone substantial upgrades and improvements. This paper discusses the CMS detector as it is configured for the third data-taking period of the CERN LHC, Run 3 , which started in 2022. The entire silicon pixel tracking detector was replaced.

arxiv-2405-20392.title: Can No-Reference Quality-Assessment Methods Serve as Perceptual Losses for Super-Resolution? Thanks: 1 These authors contributed equally to this work
arxiv-2405-20392.creator: Egor Kashkarov 1 Egor Chistov 1 Ivan Molodetskikh Dmitriy Vatolin
arxiv-2405-20392.description: Abstract Perceptual losses play an important role in constructing deep-neural-network-based methods by increasing the naturalness and realism of processed images and videos. Use of perceptual losses is often limited to LPIPS, a full-reference method. Even though deep no-reference image-quality-assessment methods are excellent at predicting human judgment, little research has examined their incorporation in loss functions.

arxiv-2505-02245.title: Intermediate-mass black holes and contribution to extragalactic background light from Population III stars in Milky Way-like galaxies
arxiv-2505-02245.creator: A. Mkrtchyan, D. Horns
arxiv-2505-02245.description: Abstract The mass range of observed black holes extends from stellar-mass to supermassive scales, yet the existence of objects in the intermediate-mass range of 10 2 − 10 5 ​ M ⊙ 10^{2}-10^{5}$\text{\,}\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ remains unconfirmed. Black holes are suspected to compress the surrounding dark matter distribution, forming a “spike”.

doe-osti-2575626-solar-tool-capacity-bui.creator: Beshilas, Laura A.
doe-osti-2575626-solar-tool-capacity-bui.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. The "Solar Tool Capacity Building for Midwestern Tribes" project sought to overcome barriers hindering Tribal solar deployment by providing hands-on, tailored solar photovoltaic (PV) and storage modeling training for Tribal environmental professionals.

pmc-11686523.title: Cervical spine infection arising from chronic paronychia: A case report and review of literature
pmc-11686523.creator: Dan Zhang, Li-Ying Gan, Wen-Jie Zhang, Ming Shi, Liang Zhang, Yong Zhang, Ming-Wei Liu
pmc-11686523.description: BACKGROUNDCervical spine pyogenic infection (CSPI) is a rare and challenging form of spinal infection that is typically caused by pyogenic bacteria and primarily affects the cervical vertebral bodies and surrounding tissues. Given its nonspecific symptoms, such as fever and neck pain, early diagnosis is crucial to prevent severe complications, including spinal cord injury.

pmc-12406294.title: Pleurotus Mushrooms in Nutrition and Health: Clinical and Preclinical Insights for Nutraceutical Development
pmc-12406294.creator: Patrícia Lima Araújo, Ediana da Silva Araújo, Erika Mayra de Almeida Barreto, José Luiz de Brito Alves, Kamylla Mylena Souza, Micaelle Oliveira de Luna Freire, Rayane Maria Pessoa de Souza, Fillipe de Oliveira Pereira
pmc-12406294.description: Pleurotus mushrooms are fungi widely consumed due to their high nutritional value and potential applications as nutraceuticals. Their sustainable cultivation and rich composition of bioactive compounds provide significant health benefits. This review examines the scientific evidence regarding the safety, efficacy, and nutraceutical potential of Pleurotus species, focusing on their effects on various human diseases.

pmc-12445888.title: Design and Validation of the Self-efficacy of Care Questionnaire for Adolescents with Mental Disorders
pmc-12445888.creator: Soudabeh Behzadi, Shahrzad Yektatalab, Marzieh Momen Nasab, Maryam Shaygan, Armin Zareian, Zeinab Rabbani
pmc-12445888.description: Background:Self-efficacy of care is based on health-promoting behaviors that are formed through dealing with disease conditions and the ability to treatment adherence and management of complications. This study was conducted to design and validate an assessment tool for adolescents with mental disorders.

pmc-12618549.title: Astaxanthin inhibits hepatocellular carcinoma by targeting USP39-mediated β-catenin stabilization through deubiquitination
pmc-12618549.creator: Xiaomei Li, Huiyuan Xu, Ruoxi Chen, Xianzhi Huang, Zequan Lin, Shouan Wang, Lihong Han, Jinqiu Li, Lihong Lin, Yamei Qi, Gang Song, Conghua Song
pmc-12618549.description: Although studies suggest that astaxanthin exerts anticancer effects through Wnt/β-catenin pathway, its therapeutic target remains unclear. The deubiquitinase USP39 may be a potential target due to its ability to regulate this pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aims to identify the role and underlying mechanism of USP39 in the anti-HCC effects of astaxanthin via Wnt/β-catenin pathway.

pmc-12649910.title: Early Taurine Administration Decreases the Levels of Receptor-Interacting Serine/Threonine Protein Kinase 1 in the Duchenne Mouse Model mdx
pmc-12649910.creator: Marthe Dias, Hanne Dhuyvetter, Ella Byttebier, Caroline Merckx, Jan L De Bleecker, Boel De Paepe, Vincenzo Di Stefano, Jinming Han, Claudia Vinciguerra
pmc-12649910.description: Background/Objectives: The progressive life-limiting disorder Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) arises from the absence of dystrophin protein at the muscle cell membrane, which leads to progressive contraction-induced damage. Despite the advancements in molecular therapies aimed at reintroducing (partially functional) dystrophin in patients, a cure for DMD remains elusive.

pmc-12698152.title: Biological Sex Is Associated with Pre-Tibial Subcutaneous Tissue Depth for Intraosseous Catheter Insertion
pmc-12698152.creator: Alex J. DuVall, Thomas Sprys-Tellner, Tristan Lemon, Ryan Kelly, Andrew Stefan, James H. Paxton
pmc-12698152.description: IntroductionIntraosseous (IO) vascular access is commonly used when critically ill patients require rapid indirect venous access for the infusion of fluids and medications. The proximal tibia (PT) IO insertion site has been shown to be associated with the highest first-attempt placement success rates. However, inadequate catheter length continues to contribute to failure of IO line placement.

pmc-13355892.title: A Bifunctional Organosilane Additive for Dynamic pH Regulation and Interfacial Protection in Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
pmc-13355892.creator: Lina Pan, Haiyang Wu, Peng Huang, Boyu Yuan, Chao Lai, Yaqian Lan
pmc-13355892.description: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries exhibit considerable potential for use in grid‐scale energy storage. However, issues such as zinc dendrite growth and the occurrence of the hydrogen evolution reaction have limited their development. To address these challenges, this study develop Ormosil, a water‐soluble organosilane additive for the electrolyte.

pmc-13632294.title: Developmental and functional landscape of theca cells in ovarian biology
pmc-13632294.creator: Mahnaz Haddadi, Samane Adib, Christiani A. Amorim, Azam Dalman, Mojtaba Rezazadeh Valojerdi
pmc-13632294.description: Ovarian theca cells constitute essential components of the follicular microenvironment and play central roles in follicular development, steroidogenesis, and endocrine regulation. Despite their significance, the developmental origins, differentiation processes, and functional dynamics of theca cells remain incompletely defined, particularly in humans.
